candidate_title: Leased task delivery with crash recovery for Huey
scenario_goal: Huey currently removes a task from storage the moment a consumer reads it, so a consumer that crashes mid-execution loses the task forever and two consumers cannot coordinate ownership. The task is to add a leased-delivery protocol: a task taken for execution stays owned by the taking consumer for a bounded lease, is invisible to every other reader meanwhile, becomes visible again automatically once the lease expires, and is retired to a dead-letter set after a bounded number of failed deliveries. Success means the storage and public Huey API expose lease/ack/nack/renew/dead-letter semantics that hold across independent connections and processes on the SQLite backend, while every pre-existing queue, schedule and result behaviour is unchanged.
actors: Producer code calling the Huey public API to enqueue tasks.
One or more consumer processes or threads pulling work from the same backend.
Operator or recovery tooling inspecting leased and dead-lettered work.
A new consumer process started after another one crashed.
domain_objects: Pending queue entries (task rows) with queue name, priority and monotonic id.
Delivery leases binding a task row to a lease id, owner and expiry timestamp.
Dead-letter entries holding tasks that exceeded their delivery budget.
Idempotency keys that pin a logical operation to at most one live task.
workflow: Producer enqueues a task, optionally with a dedup key, a maximum delivery count and a priority.
A consumer leases one or more tasks with a timeout instead of destructively dequeuing them.
The consumer renews the lease while it works, then acks on success or nacks (with optional requeue delay) on failure.
Leases that are never renewed or acked expire and the task returns to the visible set with an incremented delivery count.
Once the delivery count reaches the configured maximum the task stops being deliverable and appears in the dead-letter set.
Operators can inspect and drain leased, pending and dead-letter views.
A consumer that crashed before acking is recovered simply by another consumer leasing the expired task.
state_and_lifecycle: A task moves pending -> leased -> (acked and gone) or -> pending again or -> dead-letter.
Lease ownership is exclusive: at most one lease may reference a live task at any instant.
Lease expiry is evaluated against a caller-supplied or injected clock so expiry is deterministic under test.
Priority ordering applies to the visible set; ordering among equal priorities falls back to the original enqueue order.
A dedup key is released only when its task reaches a terminal state (acked or dead-lettered).
Lease and dead-letter state must survive process restart because it lives in the persistent backend.
conflicts_failures_recovery: Two consumers racing to lease the last visible task: exactly one wins, the other observes an empty visible set.
A consumer that dies between lease and ack: the lease expires and the task is redelivered, not lost.
A consumer that acks after its lease already expired: the ack must be rejected so it cannot delete work that already moved on.
Simultaneous renew and expiry at the same timestamp boundary.
Duplicate enqueue with the same dedup key, including after the first task was leased but not yet terminal.
Requeue with a delay must not become visible before the delay elapses even though the lease is gone.
A failed delivery that reaches the maximum count must land in the dead-letter set instead of cycling forever.
observable_outcomes: Public methods report the same leased/pending/dead-letter pictures to independent connections.
Counts and listings stay consistent with what was enqueued, leased, acked, nacked and expired.
Errors are raised for operations on foreign or expired leases instead of silently corrupting state.
Pre-existing dequeue, enqueue, queue_size, enqueued_items, schedule and result behaviour keeps working.
verifier_behaviors: Distinguish leases that hide tasks from leases that merely mark them.
Distinguish expiry-driven redelivery from explicit requeue.
Distinguish a rejected foreign ack from an accepted owner ack.
Check ordering of redelivered and new tasks under priority and delay.
Check dedup key release timing at terminal states only.
Check dead-letter transition exactly at the delivery budget boundary.
Re-read through a second storage connection to prove durability rather than in-memory bookkeeping.
task_difficulties: Choosing a durable representation for lease ownership that stays atomic under concurrent readers of the same SQLite file.
Making expiry lazy and correct without a background reaper, so a crashed consumer needs no cleanup call.
Keeping lease, requeue-with-delay and dead-letter transitions from double-counting or losing a delivery attempt.
Defining when a dedup key is released so concurrent duplicate producers converge on one live task.
Preserving the original visible-set ordering rules while introducing a second invisibility reason (lease vs. not-yet-due).
Keeping the in-memory backend semantically identical so behaviour does not depend on which backend is configured.
